argument_summary: The overbroad claim is that certification is compliant on the present record without qualification. The supportable narrower claim is that certification can be defended only as caveated compliance: the admissible evidence supports launch readiness in the aggregate and supports deployment with documented limitations and monitoring, but the current aviation maintenance triage regression is material to a named launch use case and must be reflected in the current release documentation for the certification record to align with policy. Prior approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the audit treatment is narrowed from unqualified compliance to caveated compliance tied to current release documentation. The admissible basis for that position is policy fit, not launch urgency or side-channel pressure.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not let prior approval or an informal monitoring note substitute for current release evidence or reviewed risk acceptance. But the same policy permits certification if the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and discloses the material segment weakness. On the admissible record, aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support certification only when paired with an explicit current-release disclosure of the maintenance triage weakness; they do not support an unqualified finding that the present record is already fully compliant.
concessions: The current record does not support the unqualified claim that certification is already compliant on the present record.
The aviation maintenance triage slice is currently 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold and is material to a named launch use case.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not a reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or proof that the required disclosure is already complete.
The prior approval is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
